spec.title: Example 286's fixed protected-state task through ProtectedBean's setter contracts: binding writes only what the permitted setters' proved effect contracts write (ASCII trial, bound 8)
spec.description: The state stream of the domain-advances brief, step 6 (the effect contract on 286's real path). proofs/beans/protected-setters.contract gives ProtectedBean's permitted setters (setName, setFavouriteColour, setTouchy) effect contracts: each writes its own field and nothing else that was there before the call, reads nothing that was, and leaves the String it is given. proofs/prove.py --contracts puts them beside the simpleMatch lemma; the check proves each contract first and uses it where the bean wrapper's stand-in (ProtectedBeanStandIn, sampled on 5.3.19) calls the setter, so the result rests on the setters' contracts, not their bodies. ProtectedBean has a java.util.Map field (someMap), which no property check made an object of: a write set's check now frames such a field by identity (harness::FieldKind::Reference; lib/tests/claims.rs a_write_set_frames_a_field_of_a_type_the_check_makes_no_object_of_by_identity), which is what the second use of the contract showed the first (AccountBean, String and boolean fields only) had hidden. The run is the trial of job 20261117-222610 (field also ASCII, the corrected formalization the stream proposes; the frozen claim's non-ASCII toLowerCase() is the unchanged blocker), at the claim's bound 8. A capped probe at bound 7 proved it in 93 s, naming the contracts of setName and setTouchy (favouriteColour, 15 units, is beyond the bound). Its work folder is its own; verification/.work-286/state-stand-in, which the accepted refutation reads, is untouched.
